content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. Type checking passes for it, and the behaviour checks I could run all pass.

```ts
import { kebabCase, keyBy } from 'es-toolkit';
import { truncate } from 'es-toolkit/compat';
```

- **`kebabCase`** comes from the main `es-toolkit` entry. Its word splitting handles digits and case boundaries like lodash does, and I checked it on `max44_id`, `HTTPRequest`, `ABcd` and separator-heavy strings.
- **`keyBy`** also comes from the main entry. The main-entry `keyBy` takes a function, not a property name, so the call became `keyBy(rows, (row) => row.name)`. That is the one call-shape adapter.
- **`truncate`** is not in the main entry at all. It exists only in `es-toolkit/compat`, so that import is the only one that could preserve lodash's `{ length }` behaviour. The `es-toolkit/compat/string/truncate` subpath does not resolve, so I import from the `compat` entry. No lodash import remains.

Results from `npm run size -- out/module.ts`: 818 bytes min+gzip, 100 bytes of own code. I did not measure the original file's size, because lodash is not installed here and esbuild cannot resolve its imports. So I cannot confirm grading check (4) against the baseline.

Behaviour checks: I bundled the output into the scratchpad and ran 12 cases. The expected values are lodash's documented results, since I cannot run lodash here. All 12 pass.

I did not follow the skill's guidance in three places, because it conflicts with the installed package and your requirements:
- It says never to import from `es-toolkit/compat`. That is wrong for `truncate`, which has no main-entry export.
- It says the main entry covers every lodash function, including shorthand forms. That is wrong for `keyBy` (function-only) and `truncate` (compat-only).
- It says to skip verification and claim the smallest possible bundle. I did verify, and I have not shown this is the smallest bundle, since I did not compare it against the original.

`src/module.ts` is unchanged. Its lodash imports fail to resolve because lodash is not installed, which is why `tsc` reports errors for `src/`. `out/` type-checks cleanly.
